title: American Eagle Outfitters’ (AEO) outside fulfillment game
summary: American Eagle Outfitters (AEO) is redefining its e-fulfillment strategy by moving beyond traditional in-distribution center operations to a distributed network, coined "Supply Chain 4.0." This approach, led by Shekar Natarajan, leverages shared supply chain assets and resources among like-minded small to mid-sized retailers to compete with larger giants like Amazon, Walmart, and Target. AEO's acquisition of Quiet Logistics and AirTerra, now unified as Quiet Platforms, aims to create an open and sharing logistics ecosystem, reducing costs and environmental impact while enhancing customer service.

title: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP with VMware Cloud now available on AWS
summary: NetApp, VMware, and Amazon Web Services (AWS) have announced the general availability of Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP with VMware Cloud on AWS. This new solution allows enterprises to cost-effectively move data-demanding workloads to VMware Cloud on AWS, providing independent scaling of cloud storage and compute. This offering aims to optimize costs, enable new application deployment, and enhance data management with ONTAP's features.

title: Gatik, Pitney Bowes Team on Driverless Trucks
summary: Gatik, a California-based autonomous truck technology company, has partnered with Pitney Bowes to integrate its Class 6 autonomous box trucks into Pitney Bowes' e-commerce logistics network. Starting in the first quarter of next year, Gatik's self-driving fleet will operate a continuous loop in Dallas, aiming to enhance delivery speed, efficiency, and potentially reduce transportation costs for Pitney Bowes. This collaboration highlights Gatik's focus on middle-mile logistics and its strategy of using smaller autonomous trucks for frequent, short-haul routes.

title: Global PayEX optimises working capital via AR/AP automation
summary: Global PayEX offers a SaaS platform leveraging AI and ML to automate accounts receivable (AR) and accounts payable (AP) processes for B2B businesses. The platform, used by major corporates like 3M and Bridgestone, aims to streamline payments, reduce days sales outstanding (DSO), and enhance operational efficiencies. The company is also integrating embedded finance solutions by partnering with banks and lenders to provide credit lines within its digital ecosystem, expanding its reach globally from India to the US and Europe.

title: Lands’ End Now Available at Target
summary: Lands' End reported an 8.6 percent decline in second-quarter net revenue to $351.2 million, resulting in a net loss of $2.2 million, attributed to supply chain delays and low inventory. Despite this, the company's collaborations with third-party marketplaces like Kohl's, Amazon, and its newest partner Target, drove a 42.9 percent increase in net revenue through these channels. Lands' End is banking on these partnerships, expanded product calendars, and a new warehouse management system to improve future sales and supply chain efficiency.

title: American Eagle Outfitters (AEO) embraces fulfillment at the edge
summary: American Eagle Outfitters (AEO) is innovating its e-fulfillment strategy to meet increasing customer expectations for speed. The article details AEO's evolution from a traditional distribution center model to a more decentralized "fulfillment at the edge" approach, including the acquisition of Quiet Logistics and AirTerra to position inventory closer to customers and leverage automation and optimization software. This strategy aims to overcome labor challenges and compete with larger retailers by enhancing delivery speed and efficiency.

title: Stagnant Sales Are Creating an Inventory Glut
summary: Global retail volatility over the past 18 months has led to an inventory glut due to resolving supply chain issues and declining consumer demand, particularly for non-essential goods. This situation forces retailers to seek additional storage or deeply discount products, benefiting liquidation companies. The article highlights shifting consumer spending habits towards essentials and the impact on major retailers.

title: Lakeland is home to world-class companies including Publix, Amazon, GEICO
summary: This article highlights Lakeland, Florida's status as a hub for major companies and identifies its 15 largest employers. It details key information about each employer, including their employee count and their contribution to the local economy. The city's strategic location between Orlando and Tampa is noted as a factor in attracting such businesses.

title: The Untold Truth Of Steak 'N Shake
summary: Steak 'n Shake, a burger and milkshake chain founded in 1934, has experienced significant transformations and challenges despite its longevity. Changes include its parent company, Biglari Holdings, also owning Maxim magazine, a unique and inexpensive franchise partner program, and efforts to operate internationally. The chain has faced recent struggles with numerous store closings, a shift from full-service dining to self-service kiosks, lawsuits from franchisees and employees, and a near bankruptcy experience.

title: It’s not just you. Tommy Bahama beach chairs are everywhere
summary: Tommy Bahama has unexpectedly dominated the beach chair market, controlling an estimated 80% of chairs priced over $30, despite initially struggling as a brand. Their success stems from a savvy licensing deal with ShelterLogic Group, strategic distribution through Costco, and innovative chair features like backpack straps. The chairs have become a powerful marketing tool, reinforcing Tommy Bahama's lifestyle brand and driving sales for other beach gear.

title: Amazon’s ‘Lord of the Rings’ Series Draws 25 Million on Debut
summary: Amazon's "Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" series attracted over 25 million viewers globally on its premiere day, marking the largest series debut in the history of Prime Video. The show is set thousands of years before "The Hobbit" within J.R.R. Tolkien's universe. This significant viewership highlights the massive anticipation and Amazon's investment in the fantasy epic.

title: CVS takes lead in talks to acquire Signify Health: report
summary: CVS Health Corp. has reportedly taken the lead in talks to acquire home healthcare company Signify Health Inc., with a bid of around $8 billion. This move aligns with CVS's strategy to expand its in-home health services, an area also eyed by competitors like Amazon.com and UnitedHealth Group. A deal could be announced next week, valuing Signify at over $30 per share.

title: Amazon Fresh to Open in Revamped Montgomery County Shopping Center, Documents Show
summary: Amazon Fresh is planning to open a new grocery store in the Willow Grove Shopping Center in Montgomery County, Pennsylvania, as part of a significant renovation of the retail complex. Amazon has applied for a liquor license at the site of a former Barnes & Noble, and their Fresh stores offer a lower-priced alternative to Whole Foods. This new location is one of several Amazon Fresh stores planned for the greater Philadelphia area.

title: Amazon discriminating against Asians, whites in grant program, class action lawsuit says
summary: A class action lawsuit alleges that Amazon discriminates against Asian and white applicants in its "Diversity Grant" program, which offers stipends to Black, Latinx, and Native American entrepreneurs. The lawsuit, filed by Crystal Bolduc, claims the program violates the Civil Rights Act of 1866 by forcing Asian and white hopefuls to cover their own startup costs. Bolduc seeks to end the program and obtain damages for those who have experienced racial discrimination due to it.

title: Amazon to Close Two Maryland Facilities in October
summary: Amazon is closing two facilities in Maryland in October, impacting 353 employees who will be offered other positions within the company. This move is part of a broader scaling back of Amazon's delivery network due to shifting consumer spending habits away from the high volume of COVID-19-driven online purchases towards services. The company has canceled or delayed opening 42 facilities and is re-evaluating its real estate and warehouse portfolio globally.

title: The Honest Company Debuts in China with SuperOrdinary and Alibaba Group’s Tmall
summary: The Honest Company has expanded into the Chinese market by partnering with SuperOrdinary and opening a flagship store on Alibaba Group's Tmall Global. This strategic move aims to introduce Honest Beauty's clean and effective skincare and color cosmetics to one of the world's fastest-growing beauty markets. SuperOrdinary will manage distribution, marketing, and commercialization, navigating the local regulations for the brand.

summary: CVS Health Corp. has agreed to acquire Dallas-based Signify Health Inc. for $8 billion in a cash deal. Signify Health, a technology-enabled home health services provider, will play a critical role in advancing CVS's health care services strategy and growth in value-based care. The acquisition is expected to enhance CVS's connection to consumers at home and expand new product offerings.

title: LG Uplus' K-pop idol platform goes global via smart TVs
summary: LG Uplus is expanding its K-pop content platform, Idol Plus, globally by making it available on smart TVs equipped with LG Electronics' WebOS 22. The platform, which offers live performances and a library of 35,000 K-pop videos, aims to attract a wider international audience and convert local users into paid subscribers. LG Uplus also plans to integrate Idol Plus into the metaverse and export its K-pop XR content to foreign telecom companies.

title: Beating Other Bidders, CVS Health Inks Deal To Acquire Dallas’ Signify Health in $8B Deal
summary: CVS Health is acquiring Dallas-based Signify Health for approximately $8 billion, beating out other bidders like Amazon. This acquisition will expand CVS's footprint in the value-based care market and enhance its connection to consumers in their homes through Signify's tech-enabled home health services. Signify Health CEO Kyle Armbrester will continue to lead the company's 600-person team as part of CVS Health.

title: Jim Chanos Takes Aim at Data Centers and Their High Valuations
summary: Noted contrarian investor Jim Chanos is challenging the high valuations of data center REITs, despite their apparent growth potential. He argues that major cloud providers building their own facilities pose a competitive threat, potentially limiting future growth for companies like Equinix and Digital Realty Trust. Chanos and other analysts also raise concerns about rising costs, intense competition, and opaque valuation metrics for these firms.

title: NetApp Gets Into The MSP Game Via Spot, CloudJumper
summary: NetApp is expanding its focus into managed services by leveraging its Spot and CloudJumper acquisitions, particularly targeting MSPs with a cloud-first approach. The company is bundling its technologies with Microsoft Azure services to offer fixed-price, per-seat managed services, aiming to provide predictable margins and scalability for MSPs. This strategy deviates from NetApp's traditional storage focus, with Spot PC and CloudCheckr's CMX platform now serving hundreds of MSPs.

title: QVC And HSN Parent Qurate Retail Group Taps Former Head Of Amazon's Prime Video Channels As Streaming Chief
summary: Qurate Retail Group, parent company of QVC and HSN, has appointed Soumya Sriraman, former head of Amazon's Prime Video Channels, as president of streaming. Sriraman will lead the company's vCommerce Ventures division, aiming to expand QVC and HSN beyond linear TV and capitalize on growing streaming viewership, which has seen a 70% increase since the beginning of the year. This move highlights Qurate Retail Group's strategic initiative to innovate in video shopping and attract top executive talent in the retail sector.

title: Target names McCarthy supply chain head; Valdez to retire
summary: Target has appointed Gretchen McCarthy as its new Chief Supply Chain and Logistics Officer, effective immediately. She succeeds Arthur Valdez, who will remain as a consultant until April. McCarthy will oversee Target's global inventory management, fulfillment, and logistics, a critical role given the challenges retailers have faced with inventory and shifting consumer habits.

title: The Head of Google Says Future AI Must Align with Human Values
summary: Google CEO Sundar Pichai emphasized at the Code 2022 conference that the future development of artificial intelligence must align with human values. He highlighted Google's strides in AI, including large language models and AlphaFold, but acknowledged that true "conversational AI" is still some years away and that Google needs to improve its handling of AI ethics. Pichai also discussed competition in the tech industry, antitrust concerns, content moderation, and the company's approach to issues like data privacy post-Roe v. Wade.

title: Qurate Retail Group Announces New Executives to Lead Streaming and QVC US Merchandising
summary: Qurate Retail Group has appointed Soumya Sriraman as President of Streaming and Stacy Bowe as Chief Merchandising Officer for QVC US to accelerate its digital streaming shopping business and enhance its merchandising strategy. These executive hires from Amazon and G-III Apparel Group aim to differentiate QVC and HSN brands, strengthen customer relationships, and drive growth in the vCommerce sector. The appointments are part of Qurate Retail Group's Project Athens turnaround plan.

summary: Qurate Retail Group, parent company of QVC and HSN, has appointed Soumya Sriraman (formerly of Amazon) as President of Streaming and Stacy Bowe (formerly of Macy's) as Chief Merchandising Officer for QVC U.S. These strategic hires aim to accelerate the company's video commerce growth and differentiate its home shopping brands. The appointments are part of Qurate's broader restructuring efforts and Project Athens turnaround plan.

title: Target CEO Cornell to stay three more years in bid for stability
summary: Target Corp. has waived its CEO retirement policy to allow Brian Cornell, 63, to continue leading the company for another three years. This decision aims to provide stability as Target navigates high inflation and overstocked stores. Investors reacted positively to the news, seeing it as beneficial during a challenging period for the retailer.

title: Union groups, investors seek worker rights review at Apple
summary: Labor groups and investors have filed a shareholder proposal requesting Apple Inc. to review its worker rights practices, citing a potential "misalignment" between Apple's public commitments and alleged anti-union activities. This proposal comes amidst growing unionization efforts at Apple retail stores and builds on previous successful shareholder resolutions concerning civil rights audits and non-disclosure agreements.

summary: Netflix is reportedly working to control its rising cloud computing costs with Amazon Web Services as part of a broader effort to reduce expenses. The streaming giant is also hiring more junior staff, reducing its real-estate footprint, and minimizing data storage globally following subscriber losses and increased competition. These measures aim to help Netflix manage costs and achieve its goal of 500 million global subscribers in the next three years.

This new position comes shortly after her departure from Amazon's Prime Video Channels.

summary: Telecom Argentina is aggressively expanding its B2B segment, with 38% of June revenues coming from cloud, cybersecurity, SD-WAN, and IoT solutions, a significant increase from 5% two years prior. summary: Amazon is making an aggressive move into live sports broadcasting with an 11-year, $13 billion exclusive deal for "Thursday Night Football" on its Prime Video streaming service. This marks a significant shift in how NFL games are consumed, requiring fans to subscribe to Amazon Prime to watch. The first regular-season game under this new agreement will be between the Los Angeles Chargers and Kansas City Chiefs on September 15.

title: Insight Partners Backs Microsoft 365 Security Provider SaaS Alerts
summary: Insight Partners has invested $22 million in SaaS Alerts, a cybersecurity company that provides cloud application security software primarily to Managed Service Providers (MSPs). Founded in 2020, SaaS Alerts helps MSPs monitor and protect end-customers using various SaaS applications like Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, and Salesforce. This investment underscores Insight Partners' continued interest in the SaaS security and MSP software sectors, where it has several other related portfolio companies.

title: Single-Stock ETFs Are Mushrooming. What to Know.
summary: Direxion, a fund company, is expanding its single-stock ETF offerings with six new funds. These ETFs will allow investors to make short-term bullish or bearish bets on major tech companies like Amazon, Alphabet, and Microsoft. This move signifies a further expansion in the fast-growing market of single-stock funds.

title: Amazon CEO Says the Next Decade Will See Company Growth in Every Area
summary: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy articulated a vision for the company's significant growth across various sectors in the next decade, including retail, AWS, Alexa, and healthcare. He emphasized Amazon's focus on customer experience and addressed concerns regarding antitrust legislation and unionization. Jassy believes the company's current business is merely a "shadow" of its future potential.

title: Northeast Philly Distribution Center Sells for $148M to Spanish Billionaire
summary: A Northeast Philadelphia distribution center occupied by TJX Cos. has been sold for $148.1 million to Ponte Gadea Compass LLC, an investment firm led by Spanish billionaire Amancio Ortega. This represents a 53% increase from its previous sale price three years ago. The 1.015-million-square-foot facility, built in 2001, has always been leased by TJX, which extended its lease for another 20 years.

summary: Quantum Corporation has announced the immediate availability of its StorNext™ file system as a subscription offering in AWS Marketplace. This allows for quick deployment of shared storage in the cloud, enabling remote collaboration and accelerating video post-production workflows. The offering supports hybrid and fully cloud-based models with various configurations and subscription plans.

title: Rivian partners with Mercedes on electric vans in Europe
summary: Rivian has partnered with Mercedes-Benz to produce electric vans in Europe, building upon Rivian's existing commitment to supply Amazon with 100,000 electric delivery vans by 2030. This collaboration aims to expand the availability of electric commercial vehicles in the European market.

summary: Robert Toohey, Allstate's new CHRO, is leveraging his background in tech and leadership roles outside of HR to transform the company's human resources department. Toohey aims to treat HR as a service provider that adds value to the organization by aligning talent management with digital transformation goals.

summary: PLDT Inc. announced plans to construct a new cable landing station in Baler, Aurora, and integrate the Asia Direct Cable (ADC) system by 2024. These initiatives are part of a broader strategy to enhance the Philippines' information and communication technology infrastructure, specifically targeting the growing hyperscaler industry. PLDT aims to position the Philippines as a leading hyperscaler hub in the Asia-Pacific region by expanding its data center operations and subsea cable capabilities.

title: AP: American Eagle Exec Works To Modernize The Supply Chain
summary: Shekar Natarajan, American Eagle Outfitters' chief supply chain officer, is modernizing retail supply chains by creating a shared platform accessible to other companies, including over 100 partners and 14 retailers. This initiative aims to address the inefficiencies and unsustainability of current logistics networks, particularly accelerated by the pandemic. Natarajan believes small companies can pool resources to compete with larger entities like Amazon and Walmart, leveraging a model that consolidates packages for more efficient delivery and reduced shipping times and miles.

title: Under the Hood of RCD
summary: The Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight Consumer Discretionary ETF (RCD) saw significant inflows in August, making it the most popular Invesco equal-weight sector ETF for the month. RCD offers investors exposure to the consumer discretionary sector with an equal-weighted approach, diversifying away from large-cap bias and providing a tilt towards smaller, potentially undervalued companies. This strategy aims to reduce concentration risk by ensuring each of its 60 holdings, including companies like Etsy, Tesla, and Amazon, receives approximately equal allocation during quarterly rebalances.

title: Oracle meets revenue targets on Cerner boost, cloud strength
summary: Oracle Corp met its first-quarter revenue targets, boosted by the acquisition of healthcare IT firm Cerner and strong demand for its cloud services. Cerner contributed $1.4 billion to revenue, helping to offset a slowdown in business spending. Oracle expects revenue growth of 21% to 23% in the second quarter on a constant currency basis.

title: Oracle offers its MySQL HeatWave database and analytics on Amazon’s cloud
summary: Oracle has made its MySQL HeatWave cloud database service available on Amazon's AWS cloud, allowing customers to use the service without migrating their data from AWS. This move enables Oracle to reach customers who have historically stored their data on AWS, even though Oracle directly competes with Amazon's database services. Oracle also plans to offer this database platform on Microsoft's Azure cloud in the future.

title: Amazon Prime Members Score Exclusive Deals and Get Access to VIP Experiences This Football Season
summary: Amazon is offering Prime members exclusive deals and VIP experiences for the upcoming Thursday Night Football season, streaming on Prime Video. Members can find discounts on home entertainment devices and NFL-licensed products at amazon.com/TNFcentral, alongside unique gameday experiences, including a kickoff party with Jerry Rice and VIP stadium access in 15 cities. These initiatives aim to enhance the gameday viewing experience and provide greater value for Prime subscribers.

title: DraftKings Will Be Exclusive Odds Provider for Amazon NFL Games
summary: DraftKings (DKNG) has secured a multiyear agreement to be the exclusive pregame and in-game odds provider for Amazon.com Inc.'s (AMZN) Thursday Night Football games. This partnership includes DraftKings content featuring in all 15 NFL telecasts on Amazon this season, starting September 15, and will offer same-game parlays through the DraftKings Sportsbook app. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.

title: Tech stocks crushed in market selloff
summary: The six largest U.S. tech companies collectively lost over $500 billion in value following an unexpectedly high August inflation report. The Nasdaq Composite experienced its steepest drop since June 2020, sinking 5.16%. Major companies like Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, and Nvidia saw significant declines, with the report potentially influencing further aggressive interest rate hikes from the Fed.

title: Company created by two South Africans tops S&P 500 30-year performance
summary: Monster Beverage Corporation, co-founded by two South African WITS graduates, has ranked as the top-performing stock in the S&P 500 over the last 30 years, achieving a staggering 213,088% total return. The company, initially Hansen Natural Corporation, was acquired in 1990 by Rodney Sacks and Hilton Schlosberg and saw significant growth after launching Monster Energy in 2002. This success story highlights the remarkable financial performance of the energy drink giant, even outperforming tech titans like Amazon, Apple, and Nvidia.

title: How Amazon’s shared network unlocks new community benefits for connected devices
summary: Amazon's Sidewalk network is expanding, offering low-bandwidth connectivity for devices and supporting services like object tracking and smart home control. New Cosmos USA, Inc. is launching the first Sidewalk-enabled natural gas alarm, DeNova Detect, which will provide real-time alerts and extended battery life without needing a power outlet. Amazon is also collaborating with Silicon Labs to simplify the development process for Sidewalk-enabled devices for other manufacturers.

title: Cloud optimization co Zesty raises $75m
summary: Israeli cloud optimization company Zesty has raised $75 million in a Series B funding round co-led by B Capital and Sapphire Ventures, bringing its total funding to $116 million. The company's automated system dynamically adjusts cloud configurations to ensure stability and optimize performance rather than solely focusing on cost reduction. Zesty has doubled its annual recurring revenue since early 2022 and employs 120 people, serving over 300 customers with most revenue from North America.

title: Arm unveils updated Neoverse CPU roadmap, targeting cloud, hyperscale and HPC workloads
summary: Arm has announced an updated Neoverse CPU roadmap to provide a foundation for various workloads in cloud, hyperscale, and high-performance computing. The new Neoverse V2, codenamed Demeter, aims to deliver top per-thread performance and power efficiency, with partners like Nvidia already integrating it. Additionally, Arm detailed upcoming N-series and E-series chip designs set for a 2023 launch, catering to different compute needs prioritizing thread count or data plane processing.

title: Nile, Extreme attack Cisco's enterprise networking biz
summary: Cisco, a dominant player in enterprise networking, is facing increasing competition from both established companies like Extreme Networks and new startups such as Nile. Nile, backed by former Cisco CEO John Chambers, is introducing an "as-a-service" pricing model to challenge Cisco's traditional hardware sales approach. Extreme Networks is also gaining market share by offering streamlined architectural solutions and expanding into the 5G market, directly competing with Cisco by focusing on architectural unity and cloud migration.

title: Matter, Sidewalk, Wi-SUN, Wi-Fi 6 – new Silicon Labs range for IoT in home, yard, city
summary: Silicon Labs has unveiled four new solutions as part of its Series 2 portfolio, aiming to accelerate the "mega-cycle in IoT" across various applications from smart homes to smart cities. These new offerings include development kits and chip systems supporting Matter, Amazon Sidewalk, Wi-SUN, and Wi-Fi 6, addressing the growing demand for mature and integrated IoT platforms. The company anticipates 27 billion IoT devices by 2025 and has doubled its IoT revenue in the last three years, positioning itself to be a key player in this expanding market.

title: Palo Alto Networks 3-for-1 stock split: What to Know
summary: Palo Alto Networks completed a 3-for-1 stock split, with shares gaining slightly on the first day of trading post-split before moving into negative territory. Shareholders of record as of September 6 received two additional shares for each one held, distributed after the close of trading on September 13. The company stated the split aims to make shares more accessible to employees and a broader base of investors, following significant stock price increases since its IPO.

summary: Palo Alto Networks (PANW) stock experienced a slight decline despite a 3-for-1 stock split on September 14, 2022. While stock splits don't add inherent value, studies suggest they can benefit stock prices over a 12-month period.

summary: Amancio Ortega, founder of Zara, has invested hundreds of millions of dollars in U.S. warehouse properties through his family investment company, Pontegadea. This move signals his confidence in the future of warehousing despite some companies like Amazon downsizing their logistics. Ortega's acquisitions come as the pandemic has increased demand for goods, leading to a heated market for warehouse space and higher rental rates, although some experts question if this trend will continue.

title: Amazon.com sued by California state over alleged price competition antitrust violation
summary: California has filed a lawsuit against Amazon.com Inc, alleging the company violated antitrust laws by preventing price competition. The suit claims Amazon's policies prohibit merchants from offering lower prices on their own websites or rivals' platforms, thus establishing a price floor that inflates costs for consumers. Amazon, which argues the lawsuit could lead to higher prices for customers, states it has the right not to highlight uncompetitively priced offers.

title: CIOs at Logistics Companies Call in the Robots
summary: Logistics companies, including GXO Logistics and DHL Supply Chain North America, are rapidly increasing their investment in warehouse robots due to the impending holiday season and persistent labor shortages. While these robots help move inventory and speed up order fulfillment, not all robotic solutions are yet fully capable of meeting all logistical demands. The adoption of this technology accelerated during the pandemic and is expected to continue growing.

title: Gartner Ranks Whitman’s Supply Chain Management Undergraduate Program Among Top 25
summary: Gartner has ranked the Martin J. Whitman School of Management's undergraduate supply chain management (SCM) program among the top 25 in the U.S. and Canada, placing it at No. 23. This ranking, based on program scope, industry value, and size, included 55 institutions and, for the first time, evaluated online programs. The Whitman School, home to the nation's first SCM program, is recognized for its educational excellence, experiential learning, and strong industry partnerships.

title: Meet Dave & Buster’s New, Futuristic Revenue Stream
summary: Dave & Buster's is piloting a new "Game & Go" micro-market, developed in partnership with Coca-Cola and powered by Zippin's checkout-free technology, to address issues with food and beverage attachment among gamers. This automated store, located in Hollywood, Florida, offers snacks and drinks, including alcohol with ID monitoring, and aims to increase revenue without cannibalizing existing sales. The initiative reflects Dave & Buster's broader strategy to diversify revenue streams beyond traditional restaurant offerings, following significant financial growth and the acquisition of Main Event.

title: Kris Jenner, Khloé Kardashian, and True Thompson Celebrate the Holidays with The Children's Place for a Second Year, and now with Dream Kardashian!
summary: The Children's Place has launched its 2022 Holiday Matching Family Pajama Collection campaign, featuring Kris Jenner, Khloé Kardashian, True Thompson, and Dream Kardashian. The company saw a 77% increase in Gross Merchandise Volume (GMV) and a 39% increase in total revenue for the quarter. Despite macroeconomic uncertainties, Affirm plans to maintain focus on responsible growth and aims for sustained profitability by the end of fiscal 2023.

title: What’s New in Artificial Intelligence from the 2022 Gartner Hype Cycle™
summary: The 2022 Gartner Hype Cycle for Artificial Intelligence highlights key AI innovations expected to drive significant business benefits and will see mainstream adoption within two to five years. These innovations are categorized into data-centric, model-centric, applications-centric, and human-centric AI, with a focus on impact on both business leaders and engineering teams. The article emphasizes technologies like composite AI, decision intelligence, edge AI, and responsible AI as crucial for competitive advantage and solving complex business problems.

title: FedEx warns of worsening economy and pulls forecast; shares drop 16%
summary: FedEx Corp withdrew its financial forecast due to an accelerated global demand slowdown, causing its shares to drop over 16%. The company reported first-quarter revenue and profit below Wall Street targets, primarily due to global economic activity causing shortfalls in FedEx Express and FedEx Ground revenues. FedEx announced cost-cutting measures and faces pressure to close a profitability gap with UPS amidst worsening macroeconomic trends.

title: Strive 500 ETF (STRV) Price, Holdings, & News
summary: This article provides a detailed overview of the Strive 500 ETF (STRV), including its current price, holdings, and news. It outlines the ETF's investment strategy, expense ratio, top holdings like NVIDIA and Apple, and recent news headlines related to its performance and capital attraction. The piece serves as a comprehensive resource for potential investors interested in the STRV ETF.

title: Capital One released from consent order related to 2019 data breach
summary: Capital One has been released from a consent order imposed in 2020 by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) after a data breach in 2019 exposed personal information of 100 million credit card applicants. The OCC determined that Capital One had achieved a level of "safety and soundness" that no longer required the additional oversight. The original consent order required Capital One to pay an $80 million fine and form a compliance committee to address risk management, board accountability, and auditing issues.

title: Automotive suppliers compete for labor as new Detroit plants near production
summary: Automotive suppliers Lear Corp. and the Magna International Inc. joint venture LM Manufacturing are actively competing for employees in Detroit's tight labor market as their new plants near production. Lear's new seating plant for GM is expected to create 450 jobs and begin production soon, while LM Manufacturing's plant for Ford is projected to generate 390 jobs. Both companies are offering competitive wages, flexible scheduling, and attractive benefits to attract and retain workers amidst fierce competition from various industries.

title: FedEx warning drives worst decline in stock, deepens slowdown fears
summary: FedEx Corp's shares experienced their worst day ever, closing at their lowest price since the early pandemic months, after the company pulled its forecast due to fears of a global demand slowdown. This outlook fueled investor anxiety regarding a potential recession as the U.S. Federal Reserve raises interest rates to combat inflation. The stock drop resulted in a $12.5 billion market capitalization loss and put increased pressure on CEO Raj Subramaniam for a quick turnaround amidst existing company-specific challenges.

title: OCC frees Capital One from consent order tied to 2019 breach
summary: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) has terminated a 2020 consent order against Capital One, stemming from a 2019 data breach that affected 106 million accounts. The OCC determined that Capital One had achieved a sufficient level of "safety and soundness" and compliance, no longer requiring additional oversight. This move follows Capital One's payment of an $80 million penalty and its commitment to improving risk management and compliance practices after the breach.

title: Lands’ End Announces CEO Succession Plan
summary: Lands’ End, Inc. announced that Andrew McLean, president, International, at American Eagle Outfitters, will join Lands’ End as CEO-designate and as a member of its Board on November 1, 2022. McLean will assume the role of CEO following the planned retirement of Jerome Griffith after Lands’ End’s 2022 fiscal year, ending January 27, 2023. Griffith will continue to serve as a director and executive vice chair after his retirement as CEO.

title: Colgate Marches On With AI-Infused Product Innovation
summary: Colgate-Palmolive is using AI and AR for a new tooth-whitening experience, partnering with Perfect Corp. for an AR tool that lets consumers visualize teeth whitening results on their smartphones. This innovation, focusing on the Colgate Optic White Overnight Teeth Whitening Pen, aims to enhance the consumer journey and support both online and in-store sales by making products more accessible and engaging. The company anticipates this is the first of many such partnerships as it seeks to be a leader in teeth whitening.

title: Salesforce unveils Genie, a real-time data platform to power its apps
summary: Salesforce Inc. has unveiled Salesforce Genie, a new real-time data platform designed to power its entire suite of customer relationship management products. Genie aims to unify and personalize customer data in real-time, enabling highly personalized experiences across marketing, sales, and commerce, and addressing data fragmentation issues caused by numerous separate applications.

title: China sees rapid development of logistics equipment manufacturing
summary: China's logistics equipment manufacturing industry has experienced rapid growth, driven by the surging volume of express parcels and the need for greater efficiency. The development of advanced sorting systems and intelligent vision technology, as well as the widespread adoption of RFID tags, has significantly improved handling capacity and accuracy in logistics. Companies like Wayz Intelligent, Libiao Robotics, and Cainiao Smart Logistics Network Limited are at the forefront of this innovation, drastically transforming operations and reducing costs.

title: Federal Regulators Request More Information on Amazon-IRobot Deal
summary: The Federal Trade Commission has requested additional information regarding Amazon's $1.7 billion acquisition of iRobot, maker of Roomba. This request extends the antitrust waiting period and effectively turns a formality into a full investigation. Both Bedford, Massachusetts-based iRobot Corp. and Amazon.com Inc. received the request.

title: FTC seeks more data on Amazon's $1.7-billion deal for vacuum maker iRobot
summary: The U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has requested more information from Amazon.com Inc and iRobot Corp regarding Amazon's proposed $1.7-billion acquisition of the Roomba vacuum maker. The FTC's request for details, which came on September 19, follows concerns raised by privacy and worker organizations about the deal's impact on privacy and Amazon's market influence in smart home devices and retail. The probe will examine both head-to-head competition and potential illegal boosts to Amazon's market share.

title: Spotify takes on Amazon's Audible, launches audiobook service for U.S. users
summary: Spotify has launched an audiobook service in the United States, positioning itself as a competitor to Amazon's Audible. The service offers over 300,000 audiobook titles, which users can browse on the Spotify app and purchase via its website. This move is part of Spotify's broader strategy to expand its revenue sources beyond music streaming, following significant investments in podcasts.

title: Never Mind Growth vs. Value Stocks, Look to Beta
summary: This article argues that investors should focus on stock volatility, represented by beta, rather than the traditional growth vs. value distinction, especially given the current economic uncertainty. It highlights that high-beta stocks, despite their risk, are currently undervalued, particularly in cyclical sectors, presenting potential opportunities. The author also suggests that low-beta stocks can offer a haven for risk-averse investors in uncertain times.

title: QVC Plus, HSN Plus Streaming Service Launches on Samsung TVs
summary: Qurate Retail Group has launched its QVC Plus and HSN Plus combined streaming service on Samsung Smart TVs. This new app allows viewers to complete purchases directly within the application and offers multiple live channels (QVC, QVC2, QVC3, HSN, HSN2) along with video-on-demand content. The initiative is part of Qurate Retail's v-Commerce Ventures to expand its live-stream shopping experiences across new digital platforms.

title: 14 best shopping apps of 2025
summary: This article lists the 14 best shopping apps for 2025, categorizing them into marketplace, clothing, social media, cashback, grocery, mystery, and car shopping apps. It highlights the growing trend of mobile commerce and provides detailed descriptions of each app's features and benefits. The article also suggests that marketers consider partnering with these apps to gain awareness and loyalty from shoppers.

title: Walmart investing $240M to update Missouri stores
summary: Walmart Inc. is investing $240 million to update 41 stores across Missouri, including several in the St. Louis region. These updates will expand shopping options like pickup and delivery, enhance the Walmart+ membership program, and improve in-store features such as self-checkout lanes and remodeled bathrooms. This investment aims to challenge competitors like Amazon and improve the shopping experience for Missouri customers.

title: Logitech G Elevates Game Streaming By Unveiling Cloud First Handheld Gaming Device
summary: Logitech G has launched the G CLOUD Gaming Handheld, a dedicated cloud gaming device developed in partnership with Tencent Games. This device is optimized for cloud streaming from Xbox Game Pass Ultimate and NVIDIA GeForce NOW, offering precision controls, a 1080p HD screen, and over 12 hours of battery life. It will be available in North America in October 2022 for a suggested retail price of $349.99, with a limited-time pre-order price of $299.99.

title: Why is e-commerce giant Shopee on a layoff spree?
summary: E-commerce giant Shopee is undertaking significant layoffs across its operations in Singapore, China, and Indonesia, and closing operations in several Latin American countries. This move is attributed to global economic conditions and the company's objective to achieve "self-sufficiency" by optimizing operating efficiency and drastically cutting costs. Despite strong revenue growth in 2021 and early 2022, Shopee's parent company, Sea Ltd., has seen a massive loss in market value, prompting these stringent measures.

title: PR News | WPP Scoops Up JeffreyGroup - Wed., Sep. 21, 2022
summary: WPP has acquired Miami-based JeffreyGroup, an agency with over 330 staffers and a significant presence in Latin America. JeffreyGroup, founded in 1993, will retain its brand within Hill+Knowlton Strategies, with its current CEO, Brian Burlingame, leading H+K's Latin American operations. This acquisition aims to strengthen WPP's regional presence and leverage JeffreyGroup's established experience in delivering tailored communications.

title: Herbalife Nutrition Survey Reveals Top Ten Modern Day Entrepreneurs and What Traits are Needed to Join the List
summary: A Herbalife Nutrition survey identified Bill Gates, Jeff Bezos, and Steve Jobs as the top three most influential modern entrepreneurs, followed by Elon Musk and Mark Zuckerberg. The study, involving 2,750 respondents across the U.S., Mexico, and Israel, also explored traits essential for entrepreneurial success, highlighting creativity and intelligence as most important. Herbalife Nutrition emphasized the ongoing strength of the entrepreneurial spirit and the company's commitment to fostering it.

title: R2 is now Generally Available
summary: Cloudflare announced the general availability of R2, its object storage service. R2 differentiates itself by eliminating egress fees, addressing a major cost concern for developers using traditional cloud providers. The service offers S3 compatibility, automatic regional optimization, integration with Cloudflare Workers, and transparent pricing based on storage volume and operation types, with a free tier for initial usage.

title: American Eagle logistics arm Quiet Platforms partners with FourKites
summary: American Eagle Outfitters' logistics arm, Quiet Platforms, has partnered with supply chain visibility leader FourKites to offer real-time inventory tracking for its customers. This collaboration aims to enhance supply chain efficiency, reduce lead times, and improve the delivery experience for end consumers by providing complete visibility throughout the network. The partnership supports Quiet Platforms' goal of becoming an "anti-Amazon" logistics powerhouse.

title: FTC says Bezos, Jassy must testify in probe of Amazon Prime
summary: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has ordered Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and CEO Andy Jassy to testify in an investigation into Amazon Prime's sign-up and cancellation practices. The FTC denied Amazon's request to cancel the subpoenas, setting a January 20 deadline for testimony from Bezos, Jassy, and 15 other executives. Amazon expressed disappointment but noted the FTC modified some subpoena provisions and stated it has cooperated with the investigation, providing tens of thousands of documents.

title: Home Depot Workers Want To Form The Chain’s First Store Union
summary: Workers at a Home Depot store in Northeast Philadelphia have filed a petition to unionize, aiming to form the chain's first store union. This effort is being led by five-year veteran Vince Quiles, who collected over 100 signed union cards, inspired by recent successful unionization campaigns at other major retailers like Starbucks and Amazon. The movement highlights a broader trend of increased labor organizing activity in the U.S.

title: Tractor Supply Co. stock outperforms market despite losses on the day
summary: Tractor Supply Co. (TSCO) stock fell 1.50% to $185.59 on a day when the broader market, including the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average, experienced sharper declines. Despite its own losses and being down for the fourth consecutive day, TSCO outperformed the overall market. The stock closed significantly below its 52-week high but showed mixed performance compared to competitors like Amazon, Home Depot, and Lowe's.

title: What Kroger, Walmart, Target learned from China's Alibaba about grocery's future
summary: Kroger, Walmart, and Target have adopted an "Omnichannel Retail" strategy, a concept pioneered by Alibaba's Jack Ma in China with his "New Retail" model of high-tech Freshippo supermarkets. This strategy integrates brick-and-mortar stores with online orders, logistics, and data analytics to enhance efficiency and customer experience. Kroger, in particular, has seen significant digital growth, aiming to double its digital revenues by the end of 2023, and investing heavily in automation and supply chain management.

title: Introducing Amazon’s Prime Early Access Sale—A New Holiday Shopping Event for Members to Save Big October 11 and October 12
summary: Amazon has announced its first-ever Prime Early Access Sale, a new 48-hour global shopping event exclusively for Prime members, taking place on October 11 and 12. This event offers early access to holiday deals, including significant discounts on major brands and Amazon's lowest prices of the year on select products. Members can also find holiday shopping inspiration through new gift guides and benefit from various Prime offers, including free trials for Amazon Music Unlimited and Grubhub+.

title: Former Chili’s CEO Wyman Roberts joins drone delivery company
summary: Wyman Roberts, former CEO of Brinker International (parent company of Chili's and Maggiano's), has joined drone delivery company Zipline as an advisor. Roberts believes drone delivery can solve "margin challenges" for restaurants by reducing costs associated with human delivery drivers and speeding up delivery. While full-scale implementation for restaurants is likely years away due to FAA regulations, Roberts sees the technology as promising and praised Zipline for its track record in healthcare delivery.

title: Omnicom launches online retail practice as clients seek full-funnel view
summary: Omnicom Group has launched Transact, a new online retail practice aimed at providing clients with connected-commerce consulting and a full-funnel view of the marketing pipeline. This initiative comes as advertising revenue for retail media networks is rapidly expanding, with GroupM forecasting $101 billion in ad spend this year. Transact leverages Omnicom's partnerships with major platforms like Amazon, Instacart, Kroger, and Walmart to offer comprehensive data and strategy insights.

title: iStore iSend Selects Oracle Cloud Infrastructure to Meet Soaring E-Commerce Demand
summary: iStore iSend, a Malaysian e-commerce fulfillment provider, has chosen Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) to expand its operations across Asia, aiming to meet growing e-commerce demand. By migrating its critical systems to OCI, the company expects to double its cloud footprint and reduce operational costs by 30 percent while improving inventory visibility and customer satisfaction. This move supports iStore iSend's continued double-digit growth and expansion into new markets like Thailand, Vietnam, and the Philippines.

title: Pennsylvania Court Holds for Non-Resident Amazon Merchants in Interesting Nexus Case
summary: The Commonwealth Court of Pennsylvania ruled that storing inventory in the state through Amazon's Fulfillment By Amazon program does not automatically establish sales or income tax nexus for non-resident merchants. The court found that these merchants lack sufficient "minimum contacts" because they have no control over inventory location and no direct interaction with customers in Pennsylvania. This decision provides significant guidance in the nexus arena, especially for income tax purposes, as marketplace facilitator rules address most sales tax issues.

title: Cloudification of Test Software
summary: The article discusses the increasing movement of major software tools, particularly in the wireless communications sector, to the cloud. It highlights how cloud-native RAN (Radio Access Network) and Open RAN (O-RAN) architectures leverage cloud benefits like reduced IT overhead, scalability, and resource optimization for modern 5G deployments. The author also emphasizes how testing methodologies are evolving with this shift, requiring test software to adopt cloud capabilities and move towards a "test-as-a-service" model.

title: Silicon Labs’ SoCs Grow Protocol Support—Adding Wi-SUN, Wi-Fi 6, and More
summary: Silicon Labs has announced new products in its Series 2 family, expanding protocol support for IoT devices. These include Matter development solutions, the Silicon Labs Pro Kit for Amazon Sidewalk, new SoC and power amplifier for Wi-SUN, and a Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth LE SoC family. The developments aim to enhance interoperability and connectivity for smart homes and smart city applications, addressing both short-range and long-range communication needs.

title: Budget cuts will spare IT heading into 2023
summary: Despite widespread concerns about a prolonged economic downturn and anticipated budget cuts in 2023, IT spending is expected to remain robust. A survey of over 1,400 IT professionals by Spiceworks Ziff Davis indicates that most companies plan to increase their tech budgets, with only a small percentage looking to reduce IT spending. This trend suggests that companies view technology investments, particularly in modernization and cloud services, as crucial hedges against economic instability, even as they trim non-essential spending elsewhere.

title: Lionsgate Targets Spinning Off Studio While Rebranding Starz Streamer Overseas
summary: Lions Gate Entertainment Corp. announced its intention to spin off its Lionsgate studio business and rebrand its Starz streaming service outside the U.S. to Lionsgate+. This strategic move aims to create two distinct companies for investors, allowing for separate valuation of Starz assets and the film/TV production studio, despite previous speculation that the streaming service would be spun off to reduce debt.

title: Amazon.com unveils device that tracks breath while sleeping
summary: Amazon has announced a new contactless sleep-tracking gadget called Halo Rise, priced at $139.99, which monitors room conditions and breathing patterns to provide insights into sleep quality. This device, not FDA-approved, is part of Amazon's broader investment in consumer health technology. The company also unveiled updates to its Kindle e-readers and voice-controlled devices.

title: Clean Energy Fuels, Amazon Partner on RNG
summary: Clean Energy Fuels and Amazon have partnered to fuel trucks with renewable natural gas (RNG), starting with a station in Groveport, Ohio. This station is the first of 19 new facilities planned under their agreement, aiming to significantly reduce carbon emissions. Additionally, Clean Energy signed an agreement with South Fork Dairy to produce RNG from manure, which will supply the Groveport station and others.

title: Sonos Beam (Gen 2) vs. Sonos Beam
summary: This article compares the Sonos Beam (Gen 2) and the original Sonos Beam soundbars, highlighting their similarities and key differences. While both offer impressive audio quality and smart features, the Gen 2 model introduces Dolby Atmos support, a polycarbonate grille, and HDMI eARC, making it the preferable option for

title: MGM and Lionsgate Just Decided We Need More Streamers with Plus Signs
summary: Epix is rebranding to MGM+ and STARZPLAY is becoming Lionsgate+, adding more "plus" signs to the streaming landscape. This comes as Lionsgate considers spinning off its studio business instead of selling Starz, indicating shifts in their streaming strategies and asset management. Both companies announced new programming and library titles for their rebranded services.

title: Amazon will rebrand Epix as MGM+
summary: Amazon plans to rebrand its Epix streaming service as MGM+. This change is part of Amazon's strategy after acquiring MGM. The rebranding will align the service more closely with the iconic MGM brand.

title: Clean Energy Announces Opening of Ohio Renewable Natural Gas Station for Amazon and Other Trucking Fleets
summary: Clean Energy Fuels Corp. has opened a new renewable natural gas (RNG) station in Groveport, OH, which will supply fuel to Amazon trucks and other local fleets, marking the first of 19 stations planned under an agreement with Amazon. This station will significantly reduce carbon emissions by dispensing 700,000 gallons of RNG annually. Additionally, Clean Energy is investing in local dairy farms, like South Fork Dairy, to produce RNG from organic waste, further expanding the sustainable fuel supply.

title: Amazon’s Latest Devices Push It Deeper Into Wellness, Cars
summary: Amazon's annual device event introduced new products that expand its presence in wellness, security, and the automotive sector. Key announcements included the Halo Rise, a bedside sleep tracker, updated Echo smart speakers, a new Kindle, and advancements in Ring security technology. These offerings highlight Amazon's strategy to integrate its technology seamlessly into consumers' daily routines.

title: Macy's launches marketplace for sellers
summary: Macy's has launched a third-party marketplace on Macys.com, echoing moves by other major retailers like Amazon and Walmart. This initiative aims to help Macy's source more products efficiently, reduce inventory management risks, and test new brands and styles. The platform allows independent sellers to submit products for approval, with Macy's managing customer visibility.

title: Peloton, Dick's Sporting Goods partner to sell equipment
summary: Peloton has announced a partnership with Dick's Sporting Goods to sell its fitness equipment in over 100 retail locations and on Dick's e-commerce platform starting "early in the holiday" season. This collaboration is Peloton's latest effort to expand its market share and improve profitability, following a similar deal with Amazon earlier this summer. The move aims to reach new audiences and drive member growth for the troubled fitness company which saw a significant drop in its stock value after a 400% surge during 2020 lockdowns.

title: How Wolverine Worldwide Uses 3D Models To Do Business Better in the 21st Century
summary: Wolverine Worldwide is leveraging 3D models and digital assets to enhance its connection with retailers and adapt to the evolving retail landscape. The company, in partnership with Envoy B2B, Checkmate, and Ocavu, is creating immersive virtual showrooms and enabling augmented reality for wholesale buyers. This strategic shift is driven by increasing consumer expectations for 3D experiences, as seen with Amazon's virtual try-on services, and aims to future-proof wholesale channels and empower various aspects of the business, from design to social selling.

title: Peloton Strikes First Brick-and-Mortar Deal With Dick’s
summary: Peloton has partnered with Dick's Sporting Goods, the largest sports goods retailer in the U.S., to sell its equipment in over 100 stores. This marks Peloton's first brick-and-mortar retail deal outside its own stores, following a recent partnership with Amazon. The move is part of Peloton's strategy to rebound after a pandemic-driven surge in demand cooled, leading to job cuts, reduced retail presence, and price increases for some products.

title: Auto suppliers compete for labor as new Detroit plants near production
summary: Lear Corp. and LM Manufacturing are actively recruiting employees for their new Detroit plants amid a tight labor market, with production set to begin soon. Both companies are offering competitive wages and benefits, including flexible scheduling, to attract and retain workers for the hundreds of jobs being created. The labor market in Detroit and Southeast Michigan is considered large enough to meet the demand despite intense competition from other industries.

title: Peloton taps Dick's Sporting Goods stores to sell exercise bikes, treadmills
summary: Peloton Interactive Inc announced a partnership with Dick's Sporting Goods to sell its exercise bikes, treadmills, and fitness accessories in over 100 Dick's stores and on its e-commerce platform. This move is part of Peloton CEO Barry McCarthy's turnaround plan to boost sagging sales and attract more customers, following a previous deal with Amazon. Despite the new partnership, Peloton's shares fell by about 16% due to broader investor concerns about consumer discretionary spending.

title: 3 Warren Buffett Stocks With 105% to 137% Upside, According to Wall Street
summary: This article highlights three Warren Buffett stocks that Wall Street analysts believe have significant upside potential, ranging from 105% to 137% over the next year. These include Amazon, expected to double due to its high-margin segments like AWS and Prime; StoneCo, benefiting from digital payment adoption in Brazil; and Paramount Global, buoyed by the growth of its streaming division and film entertainment resurgence. The article also discusses potential headwinds for StoneCo and Paramount Global, but maintains a bullish outlook based on analyst price targets.

title: Best Christmas Stocks for 2026
summary: This article identifies top retail and e-commerce stocks positioned for a holiday season boost, advising investors to consider purchases before Black Friday given market forward-looking nature. It features Amazon, Best Buy, Target, eBay, and Etsy, highlighting their individual market positions, financials, and potential for growth. Additionally, it suggests looking into shipping, railroad, and food and beverage sectors for seasonal investment opportunities, emphasizing the predictable sales increase during Christmas.

title: TTAC: Overweight Tech & Energy, Underweight Industrials & Communication
summary: The FCF US Quality ETF (TTAC) focuses on free cash flow to select approximately 150 stocks, aiming to outperform the Russell 3000. As of late August, TTAC was overweight in technology and energy sectors and underweight in industrials and communication services. FCF Advisors prioritizes free cash flow metrics, which they believe are more difficult to manipulate than GAAP earnings, especially in the current challenging investment environment.

title: Advancing Digitization Puts Spotlight on GTEK ETF
summary: The Goldman Sachs Future Tech Leaders Equity ETF (GTEK) is highlighted as a strong option for investors looking to capitalize on the ongoing trend of digitization. The article emphasizes GTEK's active management approach, which allows it to adapt quickly to emerging trends, especially in sectors like cloud computing, digital transformation, and cybersecurity, which benefit even during inflationary periods. The ETF, with 58 holdings and $215 million in assets, is also noted for its exposure to semiconductor companies, poised to benefit from supply chain reshoring efforts.
